newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN-AMRO offers to buy out other MHB shareholders.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO offers to buy out other MHB shareholders.

text.p: The Dutch banking group ABN AMRO on Wednesday said it would seek to increase to 100 percent its recently acquired majority stake in Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB) by offering to buy out remaining shareholders.

"We will definitely make an offer to the shareholders," Michael J. Drabbe, chairman of ABN AMRO's international division, told Reuters after the signing of a deal by which the Dutch bank acquired an 89.23 percent stake in MHB for $89.23 million.
The sale leaves the Hungarian state with a five percent stake which it plans to offer to management and staff at 50 percent of purchase price.
The balance is held by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the World Bank's International Finance Corp ITPa.A.

Drabbe said the company would offer 225 percent of face value to holders of the 10.77 percent stake it has not yet acquired, including employees who take up the government's share offer. ABN AMRO's offer to buy will be valid for 90 days.
The Dutch banking group announced earlier it would invest $137 million in its new Hungarian acquisition mainly to bring in automation and boost consumer banking.
Hungary announced last month it had chosen ABN AMRO as the winner of a tender to buy the MHB stake ahead of a competing bid by Creditanstalt Bankverein of Austria.
The deal means that 85 percent of Hungary's banking sector has been privatised, the largest proportion in the former communist countries of central and eastern Europe.
The contract was signed in Budapest by officials of the two banks and Hungary's minister of finance Peter Medgyessy.
"ABN is a bank in which we find all the characteristics which make it an ideal partner for one of Hungary's largest banks," Medgyessy told reporters after the signing ceremony.
The government plans to privatise Hungary's remaining banks, starting with K&H, Mezobank and Takarekbank, within the next year, Medgyessy said.
"The signing of this deal shows the government is serious about bank privatisation," he added.
MHB is the fifth largest commercial bank in Hungary in terms of assets. It has 70 branches across the country.
